treat_bins: authors' bins in interval_lt units: <= 2 wks = 1..3, > 2 wks = 4..8; reference = pre-onset intervals in the window plus all comparison-product weeks. Nov 2: recorded in event_structure as bins [0,2] and [3,inf) with reference <= -1, assigned on event_time_authors_var = ev_lt for TWFE and imputation (exact) and on calendar rel for the DiD-averaging cells. event_pre_min/event_post_max are the superseded legacy coding (single-week path, ref -1, endpoints) and are ignored when event_structure is present.
notes: EVENT version of Table 11(a) column (2) (log Reviews). Treatment indicator post_lt = 1{interval_lt >= 1} = two_weeks_since_last + after_two_weeks_last. authors' bins in event time relative to onset (interval_lt = 1): [0,2] (interval_lt 1-3) and [3,7] (interval_lt 4-8); reference = interval_lt in [-4,0] and all comparison-product weeks. run_spec event version estimates a full relative-time path in CALENDAR weeks (rel = time_week - g, ref -1 = interval_lt 0, endpoints binned at -6 and 8) and reports the equal-weight average of rel 0..7. Authors' regression (line 111): reghdfe log_num_reviews two_weeks_since_last after_two_weeks_last, absorb(id time_week) cluster(id); no controls, no weights. Table 11(a): two post bins relative to the product's LAST Facebook recruitment post (END of the promotion), interval_lt in [1,3] (two_weeks_since_last, labelled '<= 2 wks') and interval_lt in [4,8] (after_two_weeks_last, labelled '> 2 wks'), generated at do-file lines 77-80; reference = focal weeks interval_lt in [-4,0] plus all comparison-product weeks. Sample (line 85): focal weeks interval_lt in [-4,8] (1,491 focal products) plus all 108 weeks of comparison products; 259,148 rows before outcome NAs. Onset g = first time_week with post_lt = 1 (interval_lt = 1): 37 cohorts, weeks 515-551; 11 focal products have no interval_lt >= 1 row in the window and enter as never-treated (no effect on TWFE). Data quirk: time_week is the year-week of each 7-day interval, so within a product the calendar offset time_week - interval varies by one week for about a quarter of focal rows, and 14% of rows share a product-week with another row (focal and comparison products alike). reghdfe/fixest accept this. gvar = onset calendar week computed on all rows of the window (so it does not move with outcome missingness); sample_filter tie_drop == 0 drops 128 rows with interval just before onset that fall in the onset calendar week (the switch-off rule run_spec applies to treat_var specs), moving the single-post TWFE from -0.12207 (authors' rows) to -0.11889 (run_spec rows); on the remaining rows 1{time_week >= g} equals the authors' post indicator exactly. Because of the duplicate product-weeks, the CSA step, when it is under the size guard, goes through did::att_gt with panel = FALSE (repeated cross-section), not the composition-fixed cells. Published table values are not available in the project (no article text or PDF); authors_code fields are the authors' code re-run on the package data. SECONDARY ONSET (lead's ruling): treatment timing is the END of the Facebook promotion, a second timing definition for the same products as Table 10(a); the pre-period for focal products is the active-promotion phase. event_structure.source: replication/code/create-table10-11.do lines 74-85 and 109-118 (Table 11(a)): two_weeks_since_last = 1{interval_lt in 1..3}, after_two_weeks_last = 1{interval_lt > 3} (4..8 in the window); sample keeps focal weeks interval_lt in [-4,8] plus all comparison-product weeks (trimmed window); onset = interval_lt 1, the 7-day interval after the LAST FB post; reghdfe y two_weeks_since_last after_two_weeks_last, absorb(id time_week) cluster(id). The authors' event clock is interval_lt (7-day intervals since the last FB post), not the time-FE clock time_week (year-week); calendar rel minus the authors' interval ranges from -4 to +1 weeks across rows. Bins are therefore assigned on event_time_authors_var = ev_lt for TWFE and imputation ([0,2] = interval_lt 1..3, [3,inf) = interval_lt 4..8; ref = all pre-onset intervals in the window, plus never-treated comparison products) and on calendar rel = t - g for the DiD-averaging cells. The prepared panel holds only the authors' window, so no row is uncovered under either clock ('drop' records the authors' trimming). tie_drop == 0 removes the pre-onset rows (interval -1 / interval_lt 0) that share the onset calendar week with a post row: they are untreated rows inside a treated calendar cell (g, t >= g).
event_structure.verified: Bins on ev_lt equal the authors' dummies (two_weeks_since_last, after_two_weeks_last) on every row; no uncovered rows; on the pipeline rows authors' event time >= 0 iff time_week >= g on every row. EXACT on the authors' rows: fixest y ~ i(ebin) | id + time_week (cluster id) reproduces the authors' reghdfe bins (Stata re-run) to 3.5e-15 (SE 7e-10, CSV precision), N 249444 = authors' 249444. Pipeline rows (tie_drop == 0, N 249316, 128 tie rows fewer): bins 0.0632, -0.2357 vs authors' 0.0598, -0.2388; max abs diff 3.40e-03 (3.26e-03 SD), post summary 3.13e-03 SD, all from the dropped tie rows. Calendar bins (used only by the DiD-averaging cells) would give max abs diff 7.98e-04 on the same rows. Tables: ~/did_packages/_work/mksc.2022.1353/nov2_event_time_authors_check.csv, nov2_event_structure_check.csv (scratchpad meta1/verify2_1353.R, verify_1353.R).

expected_twfe_source: Nov 2 (round 2): equal-weight mean of the two TWFE bin coefficients with bins on ev_lt on the pipeline rows (tie_drop == 0), divided by the population SD of y on those rows; authors' bin mean = -0.089500
reverse_event_flag: candidate near miss (Nov 2 audit); decision pending
event_time_authors_note: Lead decision (Nov 2): TWFE indicators and the imputation estimator's observation-level bin averages use the event_structure bins and ref on the authors' event time ev_lt (= interval_lt - 1, built by build_t11a_ev.R; the authors' onset is interval_lt 1, so ev_lt = 0 is the first treated interval); NA only for comparison products (never treated). DiD-averaging cells are calendar (g, t) cells and use rel = time_week - g_lt with the same bin boundaries. On the pipeline rows the two clocks agree on treatment status for every row and on bin membership for all but 439 of 11,541 treated focal rows.
excluded_reason: Main-text rule (Hull 2026 App. B; PROTOCOL 1): the published article (Marketing Science 41(5), 2022, pp. 468-493; papers/mksc/mksc.2022.1353.pdf, obtained Nov 4) reports the staggered two-bin regressions only in Appendix B (Tables B.1 and B.2, printed with the article); the main text discusses them in words without reporting estimates, and its own regression table (Table 7) is a single-date matched DiD around the Amazon review purge. The project's earlier copy was the 2021 MPRA working paper, which has no Tables 10-11. Moved from data/specs/ on Nov 4 (decision: 'go ahead' on the open items; the T11a reverse-event question is moot). Outputs stay in output/specs and are ignored by analysis.R.
